suppliers.whereToFind: Order online by the case, or carry cases out of a cash-and-carry warehouse. Before you order a pallet, check that the lid fits the cup: lids of one brand often do not fit cups of another.
suppliers.examples: WebstaurantStore, Restaurant Depot, Imperial Dade, Odeko

suppliers.what: Point-of-sale system, card reader, online ordering, tip and sales tax reports
suppliers.whereToFind: Compare the monthly plan and the per-tap fee on the providers' own pricing pages; on small tickets the fixed cents matter more than the percentage.
suppliers.examples: Square, Toast, Clover
suppliers.note: Seen in Square's fee table: 2.6% + 15 cents (Free), 2.5% + 15 cents (Plus), 2.4% + 15 cents (Premium) per in-person payment. Names are well-known examples from general knowledge of the New York market, not endorsements and not checked in this session unless a link is given; compare at least three quotes.

suppliers.what: Business owner's policy, workers' compensation, disability and paid family leave coverage
suppliers.whereToFind: An independent broker who insures restaurants can quote several carriers at once. The New York State Insurance Fund writes workers' compensation and disability policies for any employer.
suppliers.examples: A local independent broker, Insureon, New York State Insurance Fund (NYSIF)
suppliers.note: Seen at Insureon: coffee shops pay on average $126 a month for a business owner's policy and $88 for workers' compensation across the US. Names are well-known examples from general knowledge of the New York market, not endorsements and not checked in this session unless a link is given; compare at least three quotes.

suppliers.what: Bookkeeper or accountant who knows restaurants; free city help with leases, permits and plans
suppliers.whereToFind: Ask other owners on your block for their accountant. NYC Small Business Services gives free lease review, legal advice, business courses and a team that walks restaurants through permits.
suppliers.examples: NYC Small Business Services and its NYC Business Express Service Team, a local accountant with restaurant clients
suppliers.note: Seen on the NYC Business restaurant page: free commercial lease assistance, free legal advice, free business courses and the NYC Business Express Service Team. Names are well-known examples from general knowledge of the New York market, not endorsements and not checked in this session unless a link is given; compare at least three quotes.

suppliers.what: Monthly service by a state-licensed exterminator, with a written contract kept in the shop
suppliers.whereToFind: Ask neighboring restaurants; check that the company is licensed by the state. Expect $100-$300 a month for a small cafe.
suppliers.examples: Local licensed pest management companies
suppliers.note: Seen at a local exterminator's 2026 price guide: $100-$300 a month for a small NYC cafe, $250-$600 for a first treatment. Names are well-known examples from general knowledge of the New York market, not endorsements and not checked in this session unless a link is given; compare at least three quotes.

suppliers.what: Private carter for trash and recycling: a monthly charge by pickup frequency plus a charge by weight or volume
suppliers.whereToFind: The Sanitation Department lists the three carters authorized for your commercial waste zone and each one's maximum price. The maximum is a ceiling: ask all three for a quote below it.
suppliers.examples: The three carters authorized for your commercial waste zone
suppliers.note: Correction of the existing entry: prices added. Read through search limited to nyc.gov and the Comptroller's site (nyc.gov refuses automated requests). Business Integrity Commission: maximum $26.87 per cubic yard of loose refuse or $17.64 per 100 lb. City Comptroller's review of the zone contracts: the monthly maximum for five-day service runs from $110 to $353 by zone, and the bill is the frequency charge plus pounds times the per-100-lb rate. DSNY rollout page: sign-up in Brooklyn North and Upper Manhattan from October 1 to November 30, 2026; Brooklyn East and Manhattan Northeast from January 1 to March 1, 2027; Manhattan West and Queens West from April 1 to June 1, 2027. A worked example (my arithmetic, zone rates per 100 lb not seen): 40 lb a day x 30 = 1,200 lb x $17.64 / 100 = $212, plus $110 = $322 a month in Brooklyn North at the caps, against the pack's $250.

suppliers.what: Architect or engineer to file plans, licensed plumber and electrician, general contractor with cafe experience
suppliers.whereToFind: Ask who built the cafes you admire, check licenses with the Department of Buildings, and get three written bids that say whether equipment hookups are included.
suppliers.examples: Licensed general contractors with food-service projects; the city offers free plan examinations for small businesses
suppliers.note: Seen in a contractor's 2026 guide: counter-service cafe build-outs in former food spaces run $200-$300 per sq ft, permits 6-14 weeks, construction 8-24 weeks. Names are well-known examples from general knowledge of the New York market, not endorsements and not checked in this session unless a link is given; compare at least three quotes.

suppliers.what: Listings of operating coffee shops and built-out spaces offered for key money, with asking price, stated sales and cash flow
suppliers.whereToFind: BizBuySell and BizQuest (filter New York, coffee shops and cafes); restaurant brokers; signs in windows; ask your roaster who is selling
suppliers.examples: BizBuySell, BizQuest, LoopNet
suppliers.note: Asking prices seen in November 2026 extracts: Sunnyside cafe $385,000 with $150,000 stated cash flow; 40-year-old Queens coffee shop $235,000 / $145,000; 558 sq ft Brooklyn cafe $125,000 / $71,157 with seller financing; a cafe at $120,000 / $40,126. Asking prices, not closed sales.

suppliers.what: Commercial lease review and negotiation; asset purchase agreement, bulk-sale notice and escrow when buying a shop
suppliers.whereToFind: Free: NYC Commercial Lease Assistance Program (888-SBS-4NYC). Paid: restaurant and hospitality law firms; ask for a flat fee and what it covers
suppliers.examples: NYC Small Business Services legal providers
suppliers.note: New York guides: legal fees for a small business purchase about $1,800-$10,000; one firm publishes 0.85% of the deal with a $1,800 minimum. The pack budgets $3,500 for a lease lawyer.

suppliers.what: Filing representative for Department of Buildings and Landmarks applications; certified asbestos investigator for the ACP-5 report
suppliers.whereToFind: Your architect brings both; the Department of Environmental Protection lists certified asbestos investigators; ask other shop owners on the block
suppliers.examples: Registered filing representatives; DEP-certified asbestos investigators
suppliers.note: Only a certified asbestos investigator may file an ACP-5; survey prices of $400-$1,500 are from secondary guides.

suppliers.what: A project manager who maps your permits and coordinates pre-opening inspections; free lease review; free energy survey with equipment incentives
suppliers.whereToFind: NYC Business Express Service Team (NYC BEST) through Small Business Services; Con Edison small business program
suppliers.examples: NYC BEST, Commercial Lease Assistance Program, Con Edison Small Business Direct Install
suppliers.note: Executive Order 18 (July 20, 2026) orders a dedicated project manager for each NYC BEST client. Con Edison's 2026 small-business factsheet says incentives may cover up to 100% of eligible cost for lighting, refrigeration and HVAC upgrades. Page opened (NYC Business): Con Edison offers small businesses free energy surveys and installs some energy-saving equipment for free; the Commercial Lease Assistance Program gives free legal services to businesses that meet the provider's income requirements.

suppliers.what: Coil cleaning, gaskets, refrigerant leaks, ice machine cleaning, seasonal tune-ups
suppliers.whereToFind: Commercial refrigeration and HVAC companies that serve restaurants; ask for a maintenance plan with a set number of visits. Technicians who handle refrigerant must hold a federal certification.
suppliers.examples: Local commercial refrigeration contractors; national repair networks used by restaurants
suppliers.note: Average repair calls in restaurants (86 Repairs, 2021): reach-in refrigerator $519.05, walk-in cooler $1,000.42, air conditioning $1,019.90. Call volume peaks in June, July and August: book the tune-up 8-10 weeks before the first heat wave (facilities company advice).

suppliers.what: A licensed sign hanger who files the Buildings permit, makes the sign or awning and installs it; many also build seasonal vestibules
suppliers.whereToFind: The Buildings Department license search lists licensed sign hangers; sign shops in your borough quote the permit together with the sign
suppliers.note: The Buildings Department page says larger signs need a permit obtained by a licensed sign hanger (already cited in the pack).

suppliers.category: Licensed master plumber and backflow tester
suppliers.what: Installs the grease interceptor and the backflow device, files with the city, and tests the backflow device every year
suppliers.whereToFind: The Buildings Department license search for master plumbers; DEP keeps a list of certified backflow testers
suppliers.note: DEP requires a certified tester for the yearly test; the tester list itself was not opened.

suppliers.what: Portable ramps and door hardware, a carpenter for a lowered counter, and a web developer who can test the site with a screen reader
suppliers.whereToFind: Medical supply and ramp dealers, your contractor, and your website builder's accessibility checklist; keep receipts for the tax credit
suppliers.examples: Aluminum threshold and portable ramps; website builders' built-in accessibility checkers
suppliers.note: IRS: the Disabled Access Credit (Form 8826) is open to businesses with $1 million or less in revenue or no more than 30 full-time workers. Product prices are my estimates.

suppliers.what: A glazier with 24-hour board-up service and a gate company for roll-down grilles
suppliers.whereToFind: Ask the landlord and the neighbors; keep the glazier's number at the register, because a broken window has to be boarded the same night
suppliers.note: Gate prices from 2026 press reports ($6,000-$7,000 for one gate); glass prices from glazier guides outside NYC.

suppliers.what: Installation, preventive maintenance, emergency repair and loaner machines
suppliers.whereToFind: Your roaster first: most wholesale programs include or arrange service. Then independent espresso technicians: ask the cafes around you who answers on a Saturday. Compare the hourly rate, the minimum charge, the weekend rate and whether they stock parts for your brand.
suppliers.examples: Roaster service departments; independent espresso technicians in New York City
suppliers.note: Published rates seen: $250 an hour with a one-hour minimum on the price page of one New York City company (source link; reliability of the page not confirmed); $130 an hour regular and $260 emergency at Ceremony Coffee (Maryland); $135 an hour at Visions Espresso (Seattle). Names are sources of prices, not endorsements.

suppliers.what: Yearly service and FDNY tags; hood cleaning and suppression service if you cook
suppliers.whereToFind: Only companies approved by the Fire Department, with a certificate holder (W-96 for extinguishers, W-64 or P-64 for hood cleaning). Ask for the certificate number.
suppliers.examples: FDNY-approved portable fire extinguisher companies
suppliers.note: One New York price page lists $15-$25 per extinguisher for 1-10 units, plus a $50-$150 trip fee (a lead-generation style site: indicative only).

suppliers.what: A rented ice machine with cleaning, repairs and backup ice included
suppliers.whereToFind: Ice machine subscription companies and local refrigeration dealers. Compare the monthly price with a machine you own plus two professional cleanings a year.
suppliers.examples: Easy Ice and local dealers
suppliers.note: About $155-$250 a month for a cafe-size machine; a setup fee applies. Name from search results, not an endorsement.

suppliers.what: Lease-to-own with a $1 buyout, or a loan, for the espresso machine and refrigeration
suppliers.whereToFind: The dealer's finance partner, your bank, or an equipment finance company. Ask for the annual rate, not a factor; ask about the personal guarantee and what happens if you close.
suppliers.examples: Dealer financing, equipment finance companies, lease marketplaces
suppliers.note: Rates seen in 2026 guides: about 11% for good credit, 6-18% overall, terms of 24-84 months. Two-group machines are listed for lease from $78 to $248 a month (Kwipped). New York sales tax is due on each lease payment.

suppliers.what: A machine lent, discounted or financed by your coffee roaster, with training and service
suppliers.whereToFind: Ask each roaster you consider what it offers a new wholesale account: equipment, installation, maintenance, training. Get the weekly minimum, the price per pound and the exit terms in writing.
suppliers.examples: Counter Culture Coffee, Stumptown Coffee Roasters, Joe Coffee Company
suppliers.note: Seen on roaster pages: installation, calibration, scheduled maintenance and responsive service (Counter Culture); 24/7 equipment help (Stumptown); technical support and equipment solutions (Joe Coffee). None publishes prices or minimums. A buying guide puts typical minimums at 20-40 lb a week or $300-$600 of coffee a week.

suppliers.what: A cellular line that takes over when the cable or fiber drops, so cards keep working
suppliers.whereToFind: Your mobile carrier or your internet provider; ask for automatic failover.
suppliers.examples: Business backup plans from the large carriers
suppliers.note: $30-$35 a month before equipment and fees. Reference outages: Verizon Fios, about 4 hours across the East Coast on November 12, 2024; Spectrum in Queens, more than 15 hours for 60,000 customers in 2017.

suppliers.what: Milk, plant milk, syrups, cups, pastry and coffee from many brands on one order, restocked overnight inside the shop
suppliers.whereToFind: Search for cafe supply distributors that serve your borough; the service starts with a site visit to set up overnight access. Compare its prices line by line with your current invoices before you move everything.
suppliers.examples: Odeko
suppliers.note: Read through search summaries of Odeko's own pages and Barista Magazine: nightly delivery with no minimum and no delivery charge, supply concentrated in New York City, software that reads the POS and suggests the order. The 20% is a company claim, not an independent figure. One company is named because it is the best-known of its kind in New York, not as an endorsement.

suppliers.what: Dairy, produce, bread, dry goods and paper by truck, six days a week
suppliers.whereToFind: Ask the restaurants on your block whose truck stops there. Ask for the minimum for your address and the cutoff for next-day delivery, and read the invoice for fuel and congestion surcharges.
suppliers.examples: Baldor Specialty Foods, The Chefs' Warehouse (Dairyland), Sysco, US Foods
suppliers.note: Read through search: Baldor help center (minimums $200, $350, $500 from the Bronx warehouse; no delivery fee for business accounts); US Foods next-day page (no minimum, order by 8 pm, six-day delivery); 2025 press on congestion pricing (suppliers adding $1 to $10 per delivery; a distributor group of 200 firms asked for an exemption); a forum post from a 2021-2022 shortage in which a distributor said it could fully serve only its top 31% of accounts. Credit terms are trade practice.

suppliers.what: Walk in, load a cart, pay, drive it back: milk, oat milk, syrups, cups, cleaning supplies, with no minimum and no delivery fee
suppliers.whereToFind: Membership is free: bring your business license or the tax ID letter. Warehouses sit in Brooklyn, Queens and the Bronx, so every trip costs fuel, parking, tolls and two to three hours.
suppliers.examples: Restaurant Depot (Jetro)
suppliers.note: Restaurant Depot's membership page (through search): free membership on proof of business ownership (business license or IRS letter), no minimum purchase. Trade press in October 2026 reported Sysco's pending acquisition of Jetro Restaurant Depot; I did not check the deal's status.

suppliers.what: Shelf-stable barista cartons by the case; they need a fridge only after opening
suppliers.whereToFind: Your cafe distributor, a cash-and-carry warehouse or online by the case. Keep four weeks on the shelf: it does not spoil unopened, and shortages come without warning.
suppliers.examples: Oatly Barista Edition, Pacific Foods Barista Series, Minor Figures, Elmhurst, Califia

suppliers.category: Syrups, sauces, chai, tea and matcha
suppliers.what: Flavoring syrups, chocolate sauce, chai concentrate, tea bags, matcha powder
suppliers.whereToFind: Online by the case or through your cafe distributor. For matcha, ask the importer about purchase limits and how long today's price holds.
suppliers.examples: Monin, Torani, Ghirardelli, Tazo, Oregon Chai, David Rio, Harney & Sons, Jade Leaf, Ippodo, Sugimoto

suppliers.category: Frozen pastry to bake in the shop
suppliers.what: Ready-to-bake croissants, proof-and-bake dough, muffin batter, cookie dough
suppliers.whereToFind: Online restaurant suppliers and broadline distributors. You need a freezer, an oven and someone who starts baking 40 minutes before the doors open.
suppliers.examples: Bridor, LeCoq Cuisine, Orange Bakery, Schulstad, Pillsbury

suppliers.what: Stock cups printed with your logo
suppliers.whereToFind: Specialist printers quote by the case. Start with one-case minimums; move to pallet runs only when your logo, cup sizes and volume have stopped changing.
suppliers.examples: Your Brand Cafe, Good Start Packaging, Morrison Cup Solutions, LogoCup
suppliers.note: Read through search summaries of the printers' own pages: Your Brand Cafe (one case of 500-1,000; 3-4 weeks), Good Start Packaging (from 50 cases; 14-19 weeks), Morrison (30,000 paper cups; 12 weeks), LogoCup (50 cups; about 10 days). No per-cup price was published.

suppliers.category: Selling or giving away what is left at closing
suppliers.what: A surplus-food app that sells end-of-day bags at a third of the shelf price, or a food rescue group that collects donations
suppliers.whereToFind: Sign up on the app's business page; set the number of bags each afternoon once you see what is left. For donation, call a food rescue group that picks up small quantities.
suppliers.examples: Too Good To Go; City Harvest; Rescuing Leftover Cuisine
suppliers.note: Read through search: Too Good To Go's business page (free to join, annual fee plus a fee per bag sold, the partner sets the bag price) and a 2023 San Diego Union-Tribune report (fee about 25%); payouts quarterly. Food rescue names are well-known New York groups from general knowledge, not checked in this session.

suppliers.what: Hand-rolled bagels and rolls from a route bakery, delivered before opening
suppliers.whereToFind: Ask the delis and cafes nearby who delivers their bagels: route bakeries rarely advertise. Shipped wholesale boxes exist but are meant to be frozen.
suppliers.examples: Local route bagel bakeries; New Yorker Bagels for shipped boxes
suppliers.note: Read through search: New Yorker Bagels wholesale pages (12 dozen for $169 shipped; tiers from 6 to 72 dozen; not shipped on major holidays; a wholesale account is required); Foodomarket New York quote for cream cheese, June 1, 2026; NY1 and the New York Times on the December 2021 cream cheese shortage.

suppliers.what: Cases of bottled drinks for the grab-and-go fridge
suppliers.whereToFind: A beverage distributor or the cash-and-carry warehouse. The distributor charges you the 5-cent deposit on each bottle; you charge it to the customer and refund it on empties.
suppliers.examples: Local beverage distributors; Restaurant Depot

suppliers.what: Places to post barista and shift-lead jobs
suppliers.whereToFind: General job sites, hospitality job boards, your roaster's network, a sign in the window; always state the pay range
suppliers.examples: Indeed, Culinary Agents, Poached, Craigslist, Instagram
suppliers.note: Search-seen (secondary): sponsored posts on Indeed need a daily budget reported between $5 and $25. Prices for Craigslist and Poached were not found in this session.

suppliers.what: Weekly payroll, tax filings, pay stubs and new-hire reporting
suppliers.whereToFind: Payroll services that integrate with your register and handle tips and New York forms
suppliers.examples: Gusto, Square Payroll, Homebase Payroll, ADP
suppliers.note: Search-seen (secondary, 2026): Square Payroll $35 a month plus $6 per person paid; Homebase payroll $39 plus $6 per person; Gusto Simple from $49 a month. Check that weekly pay runs cost nothing extra.

suppliers.what: Schedules, shift swaps, time punches and labor-law alerts
suppliers.whereToFind: Apps built for hourly teams; many are free for one location
suppliers.examples: Homebase, 7shifts, When I Work
suppliers.note: Search-seen (secondary, checked by a comparison site in October 2026): Homebase Basic free, Essentials $30 a month, Plus $70; 7shifts has paid tiers from about $10 to $25 a month.

suppliers.what: A trained barista for one shift when someone calls out
suppliers.whereToFind: On-demand hospitality staffing apps; book the day before or the same morning
suppliers.examples: Instawork, Qwick, Indeed Flex
suppliers.note: Search-seen (secondary, the platform's own rate page): temp baristas in New York City earn about $24.54 an hour ($21.78 to $25.45) and the business pays a markup of 20% to 65% on top, so $29 to $40 an hour.

suppliers.what: Espresso, milk and workflow training for new hires and leads
suppliers.whereToFind: Your wholesale roaster's training lab (often free with a wholesale account); specialty coffee association courses
suppliers.examples: Roaster training labs in Brooklyn and Queens; Specialty Coffee Association Barista Skills courses
suppliers.note: Search-seen (secondary): cafe operators put a new barista on register and bar-back for two to six weeks before the bar; competency comes after about three months. Course prices were not found in this session.

suppliers.what: Free forms and model policies; a lawyer for the handbook and for any complaint
suppliers.whereToFind: NYS Department of Labor (pay notice forms, posters), NYC DCWP (protected time off notice), NYC Small Business Services; an employment lawyer who represents restaurants
suppliers.examples: NYS model harassment policy and training; DCWP Notice of Employee Rights
suppliers.note: The forms are free. A lawyer's hourly rate was not found in a public source; the $300 used in the setup list is a planning figure.

suppliers.what: A tax-free health stipend or a small-group plan
suppliers.whereToFind: A benefits broker; QSEHRA administrators; the state small business marketplace
suppliers.examples: QSEHRA administrators (PeopleKeep, Take Command); NY State of Health Small Business Marketplace
suppliers.note: Search-seen (secondary): a QSEHRA may reimburse up to $6,450 a year for one person and $13,100 for a family in 2026. Search-seen (primary, dfs.ny.gov): New York approved an average 13.0% increase for 2026 small-group plans and, as reported, 8% for 2027. A per-employee premium was not found.

suppliers.what: Employment practices liability insurance (EPLI): defence and settlements for harassment, discrimination and wrongful firing claims
suppliers.whereToFind: The broker who placed your general liability policy; often an add-on to a business owner's policy
suppliers.examples: Carriers that write restaurant packages
suppliers.note: Search-seen (secondary): small restaurants pay $800 to $3,000 a year; one broker average is $1,824 a year, another $2,655. Most policies exclude wage-and-hour claims, which are the common ones in restaurants.

suppliers.what: Free recruiting and screening, wage refunds for apprentices, city-paid summer youth workers, state hiring credits
suppliers.whereToFind: NYC Small Business Services Workforce1 centers; NYC Department of Youth and Community Development; NYS Department of Labor
suppliers.examples: Workforce1, First Course NYC, Summer Youth Employment Program, New York Youth Jobs Program
suppliers.note: Search-seen (primary, nyc.gov and dol.ny.gov): Workforce1 is free to businesses; First Course NYC reimburses 50% of training wages for six weeks, up to 210 hours; SYEP participants are paid by the city; the state Youth Jobs credit is up to $7,500 (full time) or $3,750 (part time) per hire. The federal Work Opportunity Tax Credit lapsed on December 31, 2025 and had not been renewed in the latest sources (about September 2026).

suppliers.what: Marketplaces that list your menu and send couriers; they keep a commission on every order
suppliers.whereToFind: Sign up on each app's merchant page; compare the basic plan first and read which services are 'enhanced'
suppliers.examples: DoorDash, Uber Eats, Grubhub

suppliers.what: A page where customers order and pay before they arrive, and a points program tied to the register
suppliers.whereToFind: Usually an add-on from your register company; ask what it charges per online order and per loyalty visit
suppliers.examples: Square Online, Square Loyalty, Toast Online Ordering, Joe Coffee
suppliers.note: Square Online free plan: 3.3% + 30 cents an online order. Square Loyalty: $45 a month per location up to 500 loyalty visits, $75 up to 1,500, $105 above. Prices as listed on review sites and Square's help page in 2026, read through search results.

suppliers.what: Sites where office managers order coffee and breakfast for meetings
suppliers.whereToFind: Register as a caterer on the marketplace; also offer the same boxes on your own page at a lower fee
suppliers.examples: ezCater
suppliers.note: ezCater: 15% commission on food and delivery fee plus a 2.99% payment fee; 7% for orders through your own page; its delivery service costs 10% of the food total with a $30 minimum. Uber agreed to buy ezCater in October 2026, so terms may change.

suppliers.what: Free business profiles where people find your hours, photos and rating
suppliers.whereToFind: Claim the listings yourself; nobody needs to be paid for this, and nobody can sell you honest reviews
suppliers.examples: Google Business Profile, Yelp for Business, Apple Business Connect
suppliers.note: BrightLocal's 2026 survey of 1,002 US consumers: 68% want at least four stars before using a local business and 31% want four and a half. The link is the FTC's question-and-answer page on the review rule.

suppliers.what: A background music subscription for businesses that includes the public performance licenses, or direct licenses from ASCAP, BMI, SESAC and GMR
suppliers.whereToFind: Compare business music services online; if you want your own playlists or live music, contact the performing rights societies directly
suppliers.examples: Soundtrack, Pandora CloudCover, Rockbot, SiriusXM Music for Business
suppliers.note: Service names are well-known examples, not endorsements; prices of $17-$50 a month are from vendor comparison pages for 2026.

suppliers.what: A lawyer who knows restaurants: lease terms, summonses, wage rules, access lawsuits. Also registered representatives who appear at city hearings for a flat fee
suppliers.whereToFind: The city's Small Business Services office and the New York City Bar referral service; the city tribunal's own Help Center explains hearings for free
suppliers.examples: NYC Small Business Services legal assistance for commercial leases; OATH Help Center; NYC Bar Legal Referral Service
suppliers.note: OATH materials: a free Help Center and a small-business unit exist. Lawyer prices are not published; the pack's legal_help lever uses my estimate of $150 a month.

suppliers.what: A private consultant, often a former inspector, who runs a mock inspection with the city's own scoring sheet and trains the staff
suppliers.whereToFind: Ask other owners and the restaurant trade association; the Health Department sells its own consultative inspection through 311
suppliers.examples: Independent food safety consultants; the Health Department's Restaurant Consultative Inspection ($100 new, $400 after grading)
suppliers.note: City prices seen at NYC Health; private consultants at about $350 a visit are my estimate.

suppliers.what: Every required poster and notice: health signs from the city, labor posters from the state, city and federal agencies, the model harassment policy
suppliers.whereToFind: Call 311 for the health posters; download the rest from the agencies' own websites. Never pay a mailer that looks like a government invoice
suppliers.examples: NYC Health required signs; NYS Department of Labor posting requirements; DCWP 'Your Rights at Work' poster
suppliers.note: Free by design. BBB Scam Tracker shows a New York mailer demanding $92.58 for a workplace poster.

suppliers.what: Banks and licensed lenders that make SBA-guaranteed 7(a) loans for build-out, equipment and working capital
suppliers.whereToFind: SBA Lender Match on sba.gov; ask which local banks made the most small 7(a) loans to restaurants last year. Expect to show a business plan, three years of personal tax returns and the source of your own 10%.
suppliers.examples: Community banks and credit unions with an SBA department
suppliers.note: No lender is named: approval depends on the borrower. Fed survey 2026: 42% of applicants got all they asked for, 22% got nothing; small banks fully approved 57%.

suppliers.what: Loans up to $50,000 at 8%-13% for up to six years, with coaching, for owners banks turn away
suppliers.whereToFind: The SBA's list of microloan intermediaries for New York; community development lenders (CDFIs) in your borough; Kiva for a first $1,000-$15,000 at 0% raised from your own network.
suppliers.examples: SBA microloan intermediaries; Kiva U.S.

suppliers.what: City-backed loans and free one-on-one financing help; the main fund needs 12 months of operating history
suppliers.whereToFind: NYC Business "Financing Assistance" page and the seven NYC Business Solutions Centers; staff match you with lenders at no charge.

suppliers.what: A broker who values the shop, lists it, screens buyers and runs the closing for a commission
suppliers.whereToFind: Listing sites show what similar shops ask; interview brokers who have sold cafes in your borough and ask how many of their listings actually closed.
suppliers.examples: BizBuySell and BizQuest listings; members of the International Business Brokers Association
suppliers.note: Commission: secondary sources give 5%-12% of the price, usually with a minimum; no primary rate card exists. Median time on the market for a coffee shop: 150 days (BizBuySell).

suppliers.what: Auction houses and used dealers that empty a closed shop in days
suppliers.whereToFind: Restaurant auctioneers serving the city, used dealers on the Bowery, and other owners: selling piece by piece takes weeks of paid rent but brings more.
suppliers.examples: Restaurant equipment auction companies; used dealers
suppliers.note: Liquidators say secondary-market value is far below purchase price and everything sells as-is; auction buyers pay a 15%-18% premium on top of the bid. No measured recovery rate was found.

suppliers.category: Trouble: free help before you default
suppliers.what: Free legal and financial counselling for small businesses: lease disputes, debt, closing down
suppliers.whereToFind: NYC Small Business Services (commercial lease assistance and business counsellors); the New York Attorney General's office takes complaints about cash-advance funders.
suppliers.examples: NYC Department of Small Business Services; NY Attorney General
suppliers.note: The Attorney General's 2025 settlement with one cash-advance group cancelled $534 million of merchants' debts.

roadmap.title: Decide the format: counter service, menu, seats
roadmap.text: Coffee and bought-in pastries with no cooking keeps you out of hoods, fire suppression and gas permits. Stay under 20 seats and you do not have to build a customer bathroom. Count people walking past your target corner at 8am before you count on 200 orders a day.

roadmap.title: Choose how you enter: build, buy, franchise, cart or pop-up
roadmap.text: Building in a former cafe costs the least cash but takes 5-9 months before the first sale. Buying an operating shop costs about 2 times its yearly owner earnings and sells coffee from week four. A franchise needs $400,000 or more. A cart or a market stand starts under $25,000 but depends on a capped permit.

roadmap.title: Cost every item before you print the menu
roadmap.text: Write the recipe of each drink in grams and ounces, price each line from a supplier quote, add the cup and lid, and add what you expect to throw away. A latte should cost you about a fifth of its price; a bought-in croissant about half.

roadmap.title: Add up where the money will come from
roadmap.text: Most shops open on the owner's savings and family money. An SBA loan wants about 10% of the whole project in your own cash, a personal guarantee and, since March 2026, U.S. citizenship for every owner. Keep three months of fixed costs untouched: lenders will not fund your losses.
roadmap.agency: U.S. Small Business Administration

roadmap.title: Apply for the loan before you sign the lease
roadmap.text: Ask two or three SBA lenders and one nonprofit microlender. A 7(a) loan up to $250,000 may cost prime + 6% (13% in November 2026) plus a 2% guaranty fee; a microloan gives up to $50,000 at 8%-13% for six years. Make the lease conditional on financing if the landlord will allow it.
roadmap.agency: SBA lenders; SBA microloan intermediaries

roadmap.title: Scout storefronts: look for a former cafe
roadmap.text: About 800 sq ft holds 18-24 seats. A former cafe keeps its plumbing, ventilation and bathroom: a light renovation runs near $90 per sq ft instead of $200-$300. Typical asking rents for 800 sq ft: about $3,000 a month in outer Queens, $6,000 on a Brooklyn side street, $22,000 in prime Manhattan.

roadmap.title: Check that the address is zoned for a cafe
roadmap.text: Look the address up on the city's zoning map before you call the broker. A storefront on a residential block may be legal only because an old use never stopped; if you plan beer or wine, the law also sets a distance from schools and places of worship, and the Community Board is heard.
roadmap.agency: NYC Department of City Planning (ZoLa map)

roadmap.title: Check the Certificate of Occupancy before you sign
roadmap.text: The building's Certificate of Occupancy must allow an eating and drinking place; buildings from before 1938 may need a Letter of No Objection instead. Also check electrical capacity, the grease interceptor, an accessible restroom and whether the block is landmarked. Make the lease depend on getting your permits.
roadmap.agency: NYC Department of Buildings

roadmap.title: Look up the address before you fall in love with it
roadmap.text: Search the building in the Department of Buildings records: Certificate of Occupancy, open violations, Stop Work Orders, landmark status. A building with open violations can hold up your permit, and work on a landmark needs a second approval.
roadmap.agency: NYC Department of Buildings

roadmap.title: Measure what is left for seats
roadmap.text: Before you sign, draw the room. Bar about 120 sq ft, line and pickup 70, accessible restroom 60, sinks and storage 120, door area 25: close to 400 sq ft that never holds a chair. In 800 sq ft that leaves room for about 22 seats; in 500 sq ft for six.

roadmap.title: Pick your seat count: 19 or 20 is a real decision
roadmap.text: With 20 or more seats, indoor and outdoor together, you must provide a customer restroom, and in a newly built or altered space for more than 30 people that means two toilet rooms. With 75 or more people the room becomes a place of assembly. Decide the count before the architect draws.
roadmap.agency: NYC Department of Health and Mental Hygiene

roadmap.title: Look at the entrance the way a wheelchair user would
roadmap.text: A step at the door is the most common reason small NYC shops get sued. A compliant ramp needs one foot of length per inch of height; on an older building it may reach 44 inches onto the sidewalk with the Buildings Department's approval. A small business can claim back half the cost, up to $5,000 a year (IRS Form 8826).
roadmap.agency: NYC Department of Buildings; NYC Department of Transportation

roadmap.title: Check the panel, the water line, the drain and the air conditioning
roadmap.text: Ask for the electrical panel size in amps: an espresso machine alone needs a 30-amp 220V circuit, and a service upgrade through Con Edison takes 3 to 6 months. Find the backflow device and the grease interceptor, and read in the lease who repairs the air conditioning unit.
roadmap.agency: Con Edison; NYC Department of Environmental Protection

roadmap.title: Decide on gas before you sign: check availability or go all-electric
roadmap.text: A 2017 State Senate survey found restaurants waited 68 days on average for gas service, some up to a year. Con Edison answers a gas-availability request for a food business before you sign. A coffee shop with no cooking can run all-electric and skip the wait.
roadmap.agency: Con Edison (Manhattan, Bronx, part of Queens) or National Grid (Brooklyn, Staten Island, part of Queens)

roadmap.title: Have inherited equipment tested before you sign
roadmap.text: Ask the age of the air conditioner, the water heater and every fridge left in the space, and who must replace them under the lease. Pay a technician for an hour to open the espresso machine and look for scale: $250 now against $7,600 later.

roadmap.title: Walk the space with an architect and an electrician
roadmap.text: Check the electrical panel against your equipment load, the water line, the drain and grease interceptor, ventilation, the bathroom and the step at the door. An undersized panel means weeks of Con Edison coordination; a missing drain means a heavy conversion at $400 per sq ft instead of $90.

roadmap.title: In a historic district: get the Landmarks permit first
roadmap.text: Any change to a storefront in a historic district (sign, awning, door, glass) needs a Landmarks permit before the Buildings permit. Complete applications are approved by staff in 10-15 business days; the fee is $95 for the first $25,000 of work plus $5 per $1,000.
roadmap.agency: NYC Landmarks Preservation Commission

roadmap.title: Fix the deal in a letter of intent
roadmap.text: Before lawyers draft 60-100 pages, agree in writing on rent, term, free rent, yearly increases (3% is typical), the deposit, the guaranty, what the landlord delivers, and that rent starts only after permits. The landlord usually pays the broker.

roadmap.title: Get the lease reviewed, free if you qualify
roadmap.text: The city's Commercial Lease Assistance Program gives eligible small businesses a free lawyer to review and negotiate a lease before signing; a provider calls back within three business days. It does not go to court for you. Otherwise budget $3,500 for your own lawyer.
roadmap.agency: NYC Department of Small Business Services

roadmap.title: Negotiate the personal guaranty
roadmap.text: A full guaranty makes you personally owe every remaining month of a 10-year lease. A good guy guaranty ends your liability once you give written notice (usually 3-6 months), pay rent to the day you leave and hand back the keys broom-clean. Landlords trade it for a larger deposit.

roadmap.title: Negotiate free rent and the rent start date
roadmap.text: NYC restaurant leases typically give 3-6 months of free rent for the build-out, up to 12 for a heavy job on a 10-year lease. Tie the rent start to permits, not to a calendar date: if approvals slip, the free months run out while the room is still a construction site.

roadmap.title: Add the clause that saves sales tax on the build-out
roadmap.text: New York presumes a tenant's installations are temporary and taxes the contractor's bill at 8.875%. If the lease says improvements become the landlord's property when installed, the work can qualify as a capital improvement: give the contractor Form ST-124 and the labor is not taxed.
roadmap.agency: NYS Department of Taxation and Finance

roadmap.title: Negotiate your way out before you sign
roadmap.text: Three clauses decide what failure costs: a good guy guarantee instead of a full personal guarantee, the right to assign the lease to a buyer with a written release of you and your guarantor, and a renewal option long enough for a buyer's bank. The city offers free lease review.
roadmap.agency: NYC Department of Small Business Services (free commercial lease help)

roadmap.title: Read the insurance clause and get quotes
roadmap.text: The lease lists the limits the landlord demands and asks to be named on the policy. Ask the broker what is left out: flood, sewer backup, off-site power failure, spoilage, employee claims. Give honest sales and payroll estimates: the insurer audits both after the year ends.
roadmap.agency: An independent insurance broker; NYS Insurance Fund for workers' compensation

roadmap.title: Ask the city for a free project manager
roadmap.text: Since the July 2026 executive order, the NYC Business Express Service Team assigns each new business a project manager who lists the permits you need, helps file them and coordinates the pre-opening inspections across agencies. It costs nothing.
roadmap.agency: NYC Department of Small Business Services (NYC BEST)

roadmap.title: Design and build out
roadmap.text: An architect files plans, licensed plumbers and electricians pull the permits. Budget $70,000 for a light renovation of a former cafe plus about 10% for drawings and filings. Expect 6-14 weeks for permits and 8-24 weeks of construction, with rent due once any free-rent period ends.
roadmap.agency: NYC Department of Buildings

roadmap.title: Have the city look at your plans for free before you file
roadmap.text: Small Business Services offers free plan examinations, and its client managers walk you through the Buildings process. An objection found here costs nothing; the same objection after filing costs weeks of rent.
roadmap.agency: NYC Department of Small Business Services

roadmap.title: Order the asbestos investigation
roadmap.text: In a building from before April 1987 the Buildings permit is not issued until a certified asbestos investigator files an ACP-5 report. If the old floor tile or pipe wrap tests positive, licensed abatement comes first and the schedule slips by weeks.
roadmap.agency: NYC Department of Environmental Protection

roadmap.title: File the alteration with the Department of Buildings
roadmap.text: A registered architect or engineer files the plans in DOB NOW. The fee is $225 for the first $3,000 of work plus $10.30 per $1,000 after: $915 on a $70,000 job. Approval averaged 20 days in 2025. Painting, flooring and new cabinets alone need no permit.
roadmap.agency: NYC Department of Buildings

roadmap.title: Old building with no Certificate of Occupancy: get a Letter of No Objection
roadmap.text: Buildings from before 1938 often have no Certificate of Occupancy. The Buildings borough office can issue a Letter of No Objection saying an eating and drinking establishment is a legal use. Allow at least a month, and make the lease conditional on getting it.
roadmap.agency: NYC Department of Buildings

roadmap.title: Take three bids and sign a contract with a payment schedule
roadmap.text: Plumbing and wiring must be done by licensed firms. Ask for insurance certificates naming you and the landlord: under New York's scaffold law the tenant who hires the crew can be liable for a worker's fall. Pay by milestones and collect lien waivers; hold 10-15% in reserve.

roadmap.title: Order long-lead equipment before the walls close
roadmap.text: Order the espresso machine, the refrigeration and any custom counter as soon as the plans are approved. Imported machines have carried a 15% US tariff on EU goods since mid-2025, and the plumber and electrician need the exact models to rough in the lines.

roadmap.title: Open the Con Edison account and file any service request early
roadmap.text: A new business account can require a deposit of up to twice the average monthly bill. If the panel must grow, your licensed electrician files the request and Con Edison issues a service layout: allow two to six weeks, far longer if the street side needs work.
roadmap.agency: Con Edison

roadmap.title: Ask Con Edison to pay part of your efficient equipment
roadmap.text: Con Edison's small business program covers up to 70% of efficient lighting, refrigeration and controls. Apply and wait for the offer letter before the work starts, or it does not count.

roadmap.title: File for the sign permit
roadmap.text: A sign over 6 square feet needs a Buildings permit and a licensed sign hanger. File while the build-out is under way: a sign hung without a permit can cost $6,000 after a single 311 complaint.
roadmap.agency: NYC Department of Buildings

roadmap.title: Optional: apply for sidewalk seating
roadmap.text: Sidewalk tables need a Dining Out NYC license: $1,050 for four years plus a $1,500 refundable deposit and a yearly fee per square foot. Apply early, but plan year one without outdoor seats: more than half of approved restaurants waited over 19 months.
roadmap.agency: NYC Department of Transportation (Dining Out NYC)

roadmap.title: Optional: apply for a roadway cafe
roadmap.text: A roadway cafe license is $1,050 for four years plus a refundable $2,500 deposit, a hearing notice of $500-$900 and a yearly fee per square foot. The program says review can take six months. A year-round license costs more per square foot than a seasonal one, and the structure itself runs $5,000 to $35,000.
roadmap.agency: NYC Department of Transportation (Dining Out NYC)

roadmap.title: Grease interceptor and private carter
roadmap.text: Have a licensed plumber confirm the grease interceptor is the right size. Sign a contract with one of the three private carters authorized for your commercial waste zone and post the decal: the city does not pick up business trash.
roadmap.agency: NYC Department of Environmental Protection; NYC Department of Sanitation

roadmap.title: Check packaging and trash rules for your address
roadmap.text: No foam, no plastic stirrers, straws and cutlery only on request. Find your commercial waste zone and its sign-up deadline, pick one of the three carters, and buy lidded bins before the first night.
roadmap.agency: NYC Department of Sanitation

roadmap.title: Pass the trade inspections and close out the permit
roadmap.text: Plumbing and electrical work is inspected before the walls are closed, then the job is signed off. The Health Department's pre-permit inspection needs all construction finished and no food on site. Open permits left behind become your problem at sale or renewal.
roadmap.agency: NYC Department of Buildings; NYC DOHMH

roadmap.title: Schedule the Fire Department pre-opening inspection
roadmap.text: The city's checklist has you schedule pre-operational inspections with the Fire Department. If you keep carbon dioxide or nitrogen cylinders, someone on staff needs a G-46 Certificate of Fitness: $25, valid 3 years. Operating without the right certificate is fined $1,000 to $5,000.
roadmap.agency: New York City Fire Department (FDNY)

roadmap.title: Test the backflow device and file the report
roadmap.text: Hire a certified tester for the backflow valve on your water service and send the report to Environmental Protection. Repeat every year: the city tracks missing reports from its own files, and the fine is $500.
roadmap.agency: NYC Department of Environmental Protection

roadmap.title: Pass the Food Protection Course
roadmap.text: Take the free 15-lesson online course and pay $24 for the in-person exam. A certified supervisor must be in the shop every hour it is open, so certify yourself and at least one more person. You need the certificate or a course registration to apply for the permit.
roadmap.agency: NYC Health Academy (DOHMH)

roadmap.title: Get your Food Service Establishment Permit
roadmap.text: Apply online with proof of workers' compensation and disability insurance, the sales tax Certificate of Authority and the Food Protection Certificate. The fee is $280 a year. You may open on the 22nd day after applying; call for a pre-operational inspection if you want to open sooner.
roadmap.agency: NYC Department of Health and Mental Hygiene (DOHMH)

roadmap.title: Search the name before you print it
roadmap.text: Search the federal trademark database and the state business records for your shop's name and anything close to it. Renaming after a lawyer's letter costs thousands; fighting one costs tens of thousands.
roadmap.agency: U.S. Patent and Trademark Office

roadmap.title: Buy equipment and furniture
roadmap.text: A new basic set costs about $36,500 before tax and delivery: espresso machine $7,600, two grinders $4,200, fridges and pastry case $3,800, sinks, ice machine, dishwasher, register, 20 chairs and 10 tables. Order the machine first: delivery takes 2-4 weeks. Used gear from a closing cafe cuts the bill.

roadmap.title: Book a certified installer for the espresso machine
roadmap.text: The warranty holds only if a certified technician installs the machine with water treatment. Budget about three hours at $250. Keep the invoice.

roadmap.title: Line up your repair people before you open
roadmap.text: Find an espresso technician, a refrigeration and air conditioning company, a licensed plumber and an electrician now. Write their numbers, your model numbers and the weekend rates on one sheet by the register. A Saturday breakdown is too late to start looking.

roadmap.title: Line up suppliers and the opening order
roadmap.text: Pick a wholesale roaster (many train your staff and service the machine), a dairy distributor, a wholesale bakery that delivers before 7am, and a source for cups and lids. Open accounts two to three weeks ahead; the first order runs $3,000-$5,000.

roadmap.title: Open supplier accounts and file your resale certificate
roadmap.text: Each supplier wants a credit application, often with a personal guarantee, and your Certificate of Authority number. New accounts usually pay on delivery for the first orders. Give Form ST-120 only for goods that leave with the customer: cups, lids, bags, wrappers.

roadmap.title: Set up the register and card payments
roadmap.text: A Square register costs about $900; processing is 2.5%-2.6% plus 15 cents per tap. Program each menu item as taxable or not, switch on tip reporting, and connect payroll so tips and hours flow into pay stubs.

roadmap.title: Choose delivery apps and the fee plan
roadmap.text: Basic plans are capped at 23% in NYC; enhanced plans can reach 43%. Price delivery menus for it.

roadmap.title: License the music
roadmap.text: Sign up for a background music service made for businesses, or buy licenses from the performing rights societies. A personal streaming account is not licensed for a shop, and the societies do send agents.

roadmap.title: Open a second account for tax money
roadmap.text: Sales tax (8.875% on top of every sale) and the taxes withheld from pay are not yours. Sweep them into a separate account every day. The sales tax return is due March 20, June 20, September 20 and December 20; payroll deposits on the 15th of each month.
roadmap.agency: NYS Department of Taxation and Finance; IRS

roadmap.title: Buy disability and Paid Family Leave insurance
roadmap.text: Required from the first employee and asked for on the food permit application. The employer part is about $18 a worker a year; Paid Family Leave is funded by a 0.432% deduction from staff pay (2026).
roadmap.agency: NYS Workers' Compensation Board

roadmap.title: Adopt the written policies the law requires
roadmap.text: A harassment prevention policy (state model, free), a protected time off policy, and a complaint procedure. Every employer needs them, even with one employee. Hand them to each hire and keep the signed copies.
roadmap.agency: NYS Department of Labor; NYS Division of Human Rights

roadmap.title: Set the pay ladder and the tip rules in writing
roadmap.text: Decide starting pay, the 90-day raise and the lead premium before the first interview. Write down who shares the tips and how (by hours worked), and that managers and the owner take none. Staff sign it with the pay notice.

roadmap.title: Set payroll to weekly
roadmap.text: Baristas are manual workers: payday is every week, within seven days of the week's end. Run tips through payroll, show them apart from wages on the stub, and keep every record for six years.

roadmap.title: Post the jobs with a pay range
roadmap.text: Every ad, even a sign in the window, states the lowest and highest hourly pay. Do not ask about arrests, credit or past pay. Expect a week or two to fill a barista job and longer for a lead.

roadmap.title: Run paid trial shifts
roadmap.text: Watch each finalist work a real rush for three hours and pay for it: anyone who reports for a shift is owed at least three hours. Call two references before you make an offer.

roadmap.title: Hire and train baristas
roadmap.text: Four baristas cover a 12-hour day at 200 orders. Minimum wage is $17.00; the model pays $21 plus tips. Pay for training and trial shifts, give each hire a written pay notice, and schedule to avoid overtime and days longer than 10 hours.

roadmap.title: First-day paperwork for each hire
roadmap.text: Form I-9 with original documents, tax forms, the written pay notice in the worker's main language, the city Notice of Employee Rights, the harassment policy, and a new-hire report to the state within 20 days.
roadmap.agency: USCIS; NYS Department of Labor; NYC DCWP

roadmap.title: Get Food Protection Certificates for every shift lead
roadmap.text: A certificate holder must be in the shop every open hour, so one certificate is not enough. Certify yourself and two leads: sickness or a day off should never leave a shift uncovered. Their study time is paid time.
roadmap.agency: NYC Health Academy (DOHMH)

roadmap.title: Build the schedule
roadmap.text: Cover every open hour with a certificate holder. Keep each workday inside 10 hours from start to finish, give everyone 24 hours off in a row each week, and plan who relieves whom for the 30-minute meal period.

roadmap.title: Plan your own hours
roadmap.text: Decide which shifts are yours and which belong to a lead. An owner who opens and closes every day has no slack for the first sick call. Half of restaurant owners in one survey skipped their own pay in the past year to make payroll.

roadmap.title: Train the team before opening day
roadmap.text: Budget 30 paid hours a person: recipes, the register, cleaning, allergens, and the one-hour harassment prevention training. A new barista needs about three months to reach full speed, so open with at least two experienced people.

roadmap.title: Workplace posters, harassment policy, pay-range ads
roadmap.text: Before the first hire: download the free state, city and federal posters, adopt the state's model harassment policy, schedule the yearly training, and write job ads with a pay range. Hand every new worker the city's 'Your Rights at Work' notice on day one.
roadmap.agency: NYS Department of Labor; NYC DCWP

roadmap.title: Order and post the required signs
roadmap.text: Call 311 for the free posters: choking first aid, CPR kit, food allergy, no smoking. Add hand-wash signs at every sink and keep a spot in the window for the grade card. All of it must be up before the first inspection.
roadmap.agency: NYC DOHMH

roadmap.title: Put the allergy notice on every menu
roadmap.text: State law requires an allergy statement on each menu and on your online ordering page, and a poster for staff in their languages. If you wrap food made in the shop for takeaway, label its major allergens: required since November 12, 2026.
roadmap.agency: NYS Department of Health / NYC DOHMH

roadmap.title: Make the door and the website usable for everyone
roadmap.text: A step at the entrance, a counter nobody in a wheelchair can reach, or a menu that exists only as a photo are the usual grounds for an access lawsuit. Fix what is readily achievable and claim the federal tax credit: half of the spending, up to $5,000 a year.

roadmap.title: Optional: scale inspection for selling beans by weight
roadmap.text: If you weigh beans at the counter, request a city scale inspection. You get a date within 15 days; the fee is $20 a year for a scale up to 33 lb.
roadmap.agency: NYC DCWP

roadmap.title: Prepare for a day without power, water or cards
roadmap.text: Turn on the register's offline mode and set a per-sale limit. Keep a cash float and a cash-only sign. Put a thermometer in every fridge. Know the 2-hour rule for cold food, and where the water shut-off valve is.

roadmap.title: Know what to do with a summons
roadmap.text: Every city ticket carries a hearing date at OATH. Decide who opens the mail and answers within the deadline: fix and prove it, settle, or contest. A missed hearing means the top penalty and, unpaid, a court judgment.
roadmap.agency: NYC Office of Administrative Trials and Hearings (OATH)

roadmap.title: Open your doors
roadmap.text: Open once the permit is in hand or on the 22nd day after applying. Post the permit, keep the Food Protection Certificate and the pest control contract in the shop, and expect an unannounced first inspection. Keep three months of fixed costs in the bank: the first months are slower than the plan.

roadmap.title: Soft-open, then book the $100 consultative inspection
roadmap.text: Once you have begun serving food and before your first graded inspection, the Health Department will send an inspector for $100 who points out problems and issues no violations. Fix what they find before the unannounced graded visit decides the letter in your window.
roadmap.agency: NYC DOHMH

roadmap.title: Before December: salt, shovels and a snow plan
roadmap.text: Who clears the sidewalk at 6am after an overnight storm? Put it in writing, buy ice melt, check your liability policy.

manager.note: Correction: was $4,800 (160 h x $30). A manager who runs the shop while the owner is away works well over 40 hours a week. In New York City in 2026 a manager is exempt from overtime only on a salary of at least $1,275 a week ($66,300 a year), and only if managing is the main duty (search-seen, secondary: Proskauer, Seyfarth, Fox Rothschild give the same figure; 12 NYCRR 146-3.2). $1,275 x 52 / 12 = $5,525 a month. Below that the manager is hourly: 50 hours a week at $30 costs 40 x $30 + 10 x $45 = $1,650 a week, $7,145 a month. Search-seen (primary, bls.gov): food service managers in the New York metro averaged $93,730 a year in May 2025, so $66,300 is the legal floor, not the market middle.

seatThresholds.rule: A customer toilet is required at a seating capacity of 20 or more, indoor and outdoor seats and shared seating counted together; premises that held a food permit on or before December 5, 1977 are exempt until a renovation that needs a Buildings construction permit
seatThresholds.penalty: Code 5E, critical: $300 and 10 points at each inspection ($350 and 28 points at the worst level)

seatThresholds.rule: Where customers must be given a toilet and the space holds more than 30 people, staff included, separate facilities are required; two single all-gender toilet rooms satisfy it. Applies when a space is built or altered
seatThresholds.note: Read in the 2022 Plumbing Code. No setupItemId on purpose: the engine should not block on it until the lead decides whether a second room is a separate item. A 20-seat room is over 30 people by the code's count (20 x 18 / 15 = 24, + 3 staff, + a queue).

seatThresholds.rule: 75 or more people, staff included (the occupant load, not chairs) make the room a place of assembly: Place of Assembly Certificate of Operation, yearly Fire Department permit, a second exit, outward-swinging doors. Below 75 one exit may serve up to 74
seatThresholds.law: NYC Building Code Table 1004.1.3, Table 1006.2.1, §1010.1.2.2; NYC Administrative Code §28-117.1
seatThresholds.note: Corrects the pack's entry, which read the line as 75 seats. The law counts people: seating area / 15 sq ft + standing area / 5 sq ft + staff (all read in the 2022 Building Code). 48 seats is my conversion for a room laid out at 18 sq ft a seat with a 70 sq ft queue and 3 staff: 48 x 18 / 15 = 58, + 14 + 3 = 75. The pack's maximum of 40 seats stays under it; a standing event does not. The threshold number is verified, the seat conversion is an estimate.

footfall.note: Demand = people walking the block a day (data/places.json, modelled from MTA station entries and DOHMH food places and scaled to DOT sidewalk counts: data/open/fit.json) x the share who buy here. captureRate is that share for a known, average shop with no rival in sight at the reference price; real coffee shops within 250 m (DOHMH) and playing shops split the same people, and 'outside' is everyone who buys coffee somewhere else or not at all. No public statistic of cafe conversion exists. The rate, the price sensitivity and the ramp were set on the bench (sim/calibrate.ts) against three targets: an established shop on a sound block clears a few thousand dollars a month at about $9 an order, the best price sits within 10% of the reference price, and a careful newcomer ends the first year alive but far below the starting capital. A new shop starts at 35% of its regular crowd and closes about two thirds of the gap every 75 days. Every one of these is an estimate waiting for evidence: research/prompts/80-codex-real-factors.md, part A.

light.label: Former cafe: light renovation, keeps the plumbing and ventilation

standard.label: Former restaurant or food shop: standard conversion

heavy.label: Never had food service: heavy conversion (new plumbing, ventilation, grease trap)

buildout.note: Cost per sq ft: research notes (economics.md), three columns of the 2026 opening budget. Days: the notes count 3, 3 and 6 months of paid rent before the first sale; the contractor's 2026 guide gives 8-24 weeks of construction after 6-14 weeks of permits, overlapping (contractor estimates, not official deadlines). Here the light job takes 60 days, the standard one 90 and the heavy one 180, and the Health Department permit adds its wait after the room is finished. Rent is due from the day the lease is signed.

takeover.note: BizBuySell coffee shop and cafe valuation benchmarks (seen through search on November 14, 2026; the page itself is outside this session's network): median sale price $150,000, median asking price $175,000, median revenue $375,000, median owner earnings $78,780; sold businesses traded at a median 0.41 times revenue and an average 2.2 times earnings. Restaurants in the Northeast traded at the lowest cash-flow multiple in the country in Q2 2026, 2.05 (BizBuySell Insight Report). NYC listings seen in search: a Manhattan coffee shop asking $645,000 on $135,000 of cash flow, an East Village one at $150,000, a Staten Island cafe asset sale at $100,000. The game asks 40% of a year of sales the address supports, between $80,000 and $300,000. The buyer still signs a lease (new deposit), applies for a new Health Department permit (it does not transfer), restocks and hires. awareness 0.9 and refreshDays stay estimates waiting for evidence (research/prompts/80-codex-real-factors.md, part A).

financing.name: Your own savings
financing.personalGuarantee: all of it is yours to lose
financing.note: Fed Small Business Credit Survey 2026: 54% of employer firms covered a financial challenge with the owner's personal funds. Every lender below asks how much of your own money is in.

financing.name: Loan from family or friends
financing.personalGuarantee: a personal debt to people you see at holidays
financing.requirements: a written note with interest at the IRS minimum or more
financing.note: IRS minimum (applicable federal) rates: 4.67% short-term in November 2026, 4.61% mid-term in October 2026. Below that rate, the missing interest on a loan over $10,000 is treated as a gift.

financing.name: SBA 7(a) loan through a bank
financing.amount: up to $5 million; small shops borrow $50,000-$350,000
financing.fees: 2% of the guaranteed 85% on loans up to $150,000; 3% of the guaranteed 75% on $150,001-$700,000
financing.personalGuarantee: every owner of 20% or more; a lien on your home if you hold 25% or more equity in it and the loan is not fully secured
financing.requirements: about 10% of the total project in your own cash; every owner a U.S. citizen or national (since March 1, 2026); a business plan
financing.note: Seen at sba.gov: maximum $5 million; guarantee 85% up to $150,000 and 75% above; rate caps of base + 6.5% / 6.0% / 4.5% / 3.0% by size; no collateral required by SBA for loans of $50,000 or less. Prime is 7.00%, so the cap on $100,000 is 13%. The 10% equity rule, the home lien rule and the 75 days to funding come from lender guides, not from sba.gov. Charge-offs on 7(a) loans to snack and coffee bars (NAICS 722515) made in fiscal 2020-2023 run 1.76% so far; across all 7(a) loans of 2010-2019 about one in thirteen was charged off (third-party analyses of SBA data).

financing.name: SBA microloan through a nonprofit lender
financing.amount: up to $50,000; the average is about $13,000
financing.fees: small closing fees set by the lender
financing.personalGuarantee: usually yes, plus whatever collateral the lender asks
financing.requirements: a plan and often business training with the lender; U.S. citizen or national since April 1, 2026
financing.note: Seen at sba.gov: up to $50,000, average about $13,000, generally 8%-13%, six years (seven in some 2026 SBA articles). 10.5% is the middle of the range; days to money is my planning value.

financing.name: Kiva crowd-funded loan
financing.requirements: 5-40 people from your own network must each lend $25 or more first
financing.note: Seen at kiva.org: 0% interest, no fees, repayment over 12-36 months starting a month after funding. Enough for an espresso grinder, not for a build-out.

financing.name: Community investment note (crowdfunded debt)
financing.fees: platform fee, set by the platform
financing.requirements: a public offering page and an SEC Form C; your customers are your lenders
financing.note: Seen in listings of New York coffee businesses on one platform: 10.3% and 10.8% over three years in 2023, 12.5% in 2026; one of the three did not fund. Platform fees were not found. Payment shown at 12.5%.

financing.name: Business credit cards
financing.fees: none while paid in full; often 0% for the first 12 months
financing.personalGuarantee: yes, and it shows on your personal credit
financing.note: Issuers' ranges of 16.99%-28.74% after the introductory period (NerdWallet, November 2026). Planning rate 21%.

financing.name: Equipment lease
financing.fees: documentation fee; buyout at the end
financing.personalGuarantee: usually yes; owed in full even if the shop closes
financing.requirements: personal credit; the lessor owns the equipment
financing.note: No public rate sheet found; 12% is a planning value. A roaster that lends an espresso machine in exchange for buying its beans is the cheap version of this (see D03/D04).

financing.name: Retirement savings rolled into the business (ROBS)
financing.fees: set-up and yearly plan administration charged by the promoter
financing.requirements: the business must be a C corporation with its own retirement plan
financing.note: IRS: most of the businesses it reviewed failed or were heading there, with high rates of bankruptcy and liens; the structure is "questionable". No loan payment, which is exactly why it is tempting.

financing.name: NYC Future Fund (city-backed loan)
financing.personalGuarantee: owners of 20% or more, plus a lien on business assets
financing.requirements: 12 months in business, one filed tax return, $50,000 of yearly revenue
financing.note: Interest monthly; principal only in months when revenue passes a threshold. Available from month 13: a refinancing tool, not start-up money.

financing.name: Loan from your card processor
financing.amount: offered by invitation, sized to your card sales
financing.fees: one fixed fee instead of interest; paying early does not reduce it
financing.personalGuarantee: usually none; repaid from card sales
financing.requirements: several months of card processing history with that processor
financing.note: Seen at Square: repayment is a fixed percentage of daily card sales including tax and tips, with at least 1/18 of the balance every 60 days and everything within 18 months. Square's UK example charges 13.25% as the flat fee; US offers vary and are shown only to the seller.

financing.name: Merchant cash advance
financing.fees: origination and "underwriting" fees on top of the factor
financing.personalGuarantee: common, with a lien on all business assets and sometimes a confession of judgment
financing.requirements: card sales history; no credit check worth the name
financing.note: Legally a purchase of future sales, not a loan, so New York's 16% and 25% usury limits do not apply on its face. The state requires an APR disclosure for commercial financing up to $2.5 million (23 NYCRR 600). The Attorney General's 2025 judgment of $1.065 billion against one group of funders describes advances collected by fixed daily debits over 60-90 days. The example is my arithmetic on typical broker terms.

exitWaterfalls.note: What is left for the owner, step by step, for the pack's reference shop after 12 months of trading with a $100,000 SBA loan. My arithmetic; every assumption is listed. Not legal or tax advice for the player: a list of the lines a real closing statement has.

scenarios.title: Sell a profitable shop at the median multiple

lines.what: Price: 2.0 x $116,628 of yearly owner earnings
SBA loan paid off at closing (balance after 12 payments)
Income tax on the gain, 28% (equipment and build-out were written off, so nearly all of the price is gain)
Lease deposit returned once the buyer posts its own

alsoTrue: the buyer pays 8.875% sales tax on the equipment part of the price on top
the state must clear the seller's sales tax account before the money is released (bulk sale notice, at least 10 days)
unless the landlord signs a release, the seller stays liable on the lease
median time from listing to sale: 150 days, during which the shop must keep its numbers up

scenarios.title: Close and surrender the space under a good guy guarantee

lines.what: Rent for a three-month notice period while winding down (lease-specific; planning value)
Last sales tax return, up to three months collected
Last payroll, payroll taxes and accrued pay
Equipment at auction, 25% of cost less 15% commission: goes to the SBA lender, which holds a lien
Lease deposit back (rent paid up, space empty and clean)

stillOwed.what: SBA loan balance after the lender takes the auction money ($94,779 - $7,756)
stillOwed.note: personally guaranteed; the lender, then the SBA, then the Treasury collect

alsoTrue: the build-out stays with the landlord
inventory and cash in hand at the end offset part of this
the personal guarantee on the lease ends on the day the keys go back

scenarios.title: Walk away from a lease with a full personal guarantee

lines.what: Rent for the rest of a ten-year lease, nine years left: 108 x $6,000, before yearly increases

stillOwed.what: Rent as it falls due until the landlord relets, if it chooses to
stillOwed.note: New York commercial landlords have no duty to relet (Holy Properties, 1995); in practice the parties settle for a number of months of rent, which no public source measures

alsoTrue: this is the single largest number in a failed shop and it is decided on the day the lease is signed
Chapter 7 erases it at a cost of $338 plus a lawyer and the owner's non-exempt assets; home equity is protected up to $204,825 in the city
